sources.source: Fitted to 21 T-x-y points at 101.3 kPa from Kamihama, Matsuda, Kurihara, Tochigi, Oba, J. Chem. Eng. Data 57 (2012) 339 (data public in the NIST TRC ThermoML Archive; validation/data/ethanol_water_101kPa.json). AAD 0.09 K in T, 0.0033 in y (max 0.26 K, 0.0084). Data consistency point test (Redlich-Kister fit to T-x): mean |dy| 0.003 (passes, < 0.01).

Fitted to 24 T-x-y points at 101.3 kPa from Calvar, Dominguez, Tojo, Fluid Phase Equilib. 235 (2005) 215 (data public in the NIST TRC ThermoML Archive; validation/data/ethyl-acetate_ethanol_101kPa.json); checked against Zhang et al., Fluid Phase Equilib. 454 (2017) 91. Data consistency point test (Redlich-Kister fit to T-x): mean |dy| 0.005 (passes, < 0.01).

Fitted to 22 T-x-y points at 101.325 kPa (Zhu et al., J. Chem. Eng. Data 58 (2013) 7) and 37 total pressures at 298.15 and 323.15 K, static method, with the measured pure-component pressures (Brandt, Horstmann, Steinigeweg, Gmehling, Fluid Phase Equilib. 376 (2014) 48), both data public in the NIST TRC ThermoML Archive (validation/data/ethanol_acetic-acid_101kPa.json, ethanol_acetic-acid_px_brandt2014.json); a fit to either set alone misses the other by about 3 K or 9 %. Checked against the excess enthalpy at 323.15 K of Brandt et al. (validation/data/acetic-acid_ethanol_HE_brandt2014.json). Vapour: chemical theory for the acetic acid dimer. AAD 1.44 K in T, 0.0269 in y (max 2.26 K, 0.0649); P-x at 298.15, 323.15 K (with the measured pure-component pressures): AAD 0.62 % (max 1.80 %). Check against acetic-acid_ethanol_HE_brandt2014.json: excess enthalpy at 323.15 K: AAD 107 J/mol (max 275 J/mol; data 12 to 215 J/mol). Fitted to mutual solubilities at 298-333 K (Grande, Marschoff, J. Chem. Eng. Data 50 (2005) 1324; Cehreli, Ozmen, Dramur, Fluid Phase Equilib. 239 (2006) 156), activity coefficients of ethyl acetate at infinite dilution in water at 273-343 K (Fenclova et al., Fluid Phase Equilib. 375 (2014) 347; Atik et al., J. Chem. Eng. Data 49 (2004) 1429), both data public in the NIST TRC ThermoML Archive, and the heterogeneous azeotrope at 101.325 kPa, 70.4 degC and 91.9 wt % ethyl acetate (handbook value, Wikipedia 'Azeotrope tables', from Lange's 10th ed. and CRC 44th ed.); files validation/data/water_ethyl-acetate_*.json. No open finite-concentration VLE data was found for this pair. liquid-liquid: AAD 0.0007 in x of water in the water-rich liquid, 0.0321 in the ethyl-acetate-rich liquid; gamma at infinite dilution: AARD 4.3 % (max 13.5 %); heterogeneous azeotrope at 101.325 kPa: 70.76 degC, vapour x of water 0.315, liquids 0.989 / 0.195 (target 70.40 degC, 0.301). Check against water_ethyl-acetate_lle_xu2017.json: liquid-liquid: AAD 0.0031 in x of water in the water-rich liquid. Temperature range of the data: 273.35-343.55 K; outside it the parameters are extrapolated.

Fitted to 18 T-x-y points at 101.33 kPa from Chang, Guan, Li, Yao, J. Chem. Eng. Data 50 (2005) 1129 (data public in the NIST TRC ThermoML Archive; validation/data/water_acetic-acid_101kPa_chang2005.json); checked against the 24 points at 101.325 kPa of Calvar, Dominguez, Tojo, Fluid Phase Equilib. 235 (2005) 215 (validation/data/water_acetic-acid_101kPa_calvar2005.json), which scatter more (point test mean |dy| 0.038). Rigorous absorber: 8 equilibrium stages numbered from the top, no condenser; feeds on stages 1, 8, at 100 kPa without pressure drop; every stage adiabatic. The gas leaving the top leaves by the outlet "gas out" (port id "distillate"), the liquid leaving the bottom by "liquid out" (port id "bottoms").
